title: Hyper-pipelined 20-stage branch misprediction pipeline for frequency
where_in_paper: CLOCK RATES and Figure 2/Figure 3 Misprediction Pipeline
decision: Double pipeline depth to 20-stage misprediction pipeline vs 10-stage P6, with fewer gates of logic per stage, targeting >1.6x higher frequency than P6 on same process
alternatives_or_rejected: Keep P6-like 10-stage pipeline with similar gates per stage which would give similar frequency to P6 and limit performance scaling; paper explicitly discusses tradeoff that deeper pipeline lowers per-clock efficiency but net performance still higher due to frequency
rationale: Frequency target determines gates per stage; by dividing work into smaller pieces the clock rate can be a lot higher; NetBurst was designed for industry-leading clock rate with hyper-pipelined technology to significantly increase frequency capability, even though mispredicted branches and cache misses take more cycles
outcome: At introduction 1.5x frequency of Pentium III on same process (1.3-1.5 GHz), with headroom for future scaling; pipeline can have >100 instructions in flight, 48 loads and 24 stores allocated, but mispredict penalty is 20 stages

title: Execution Trace Cache as primary L1 instruction cache
where_in_paper: NETBURST MICROARCHITECTURE - Trace Cache and IA-32 Instruction Decoder
decision: Replace conventional L1 I-cache with 12K-uop Execution Trace Cache sitting between decode logic and execution core, storing already decoded IA-32 instructions as program-ordered traces of up to 6 uops per line including branch targets even if thousands of bytes apart
alternatives_or_rejected: Conventional 8K-16K byte instruction cache that provides instructions up to taken branch but none after it, plus requires high-bandwidth IA-32 decoder capable of decoding several instructions per clock in the main loop
rationale: IA-32 instructions are variable-length and cumbersome to decode, decoding several per clock at high frequency takes several pipeline stages; by caching decoded uops the NetBurst bypasses decoder most of time, reducing misprediction latency and allowing decoder to be simplified to decode only one IA-32 instruction per clock cycle
outcome: Most instructions fetched and executed from Trace Cache (similar hit rate to 8K-16K byte I-cache), up to 3 uops per clock delivered to out-of-order engine, Trace Cache miss handled by fetching from L2 via front-end BTB/ITLB

title: Separate allocation of ROB status and physical register file
where_in_paper: Out-of-order Execution Logic - The Allocator and Figure 5 Register allocation
decision: Allocate ROB entries (status only) and 128-entry physical integer/FP register file entries separately, rather than combined ROB+data as in P6; ROB entries allocated/deallocated sequentially with sequence number for age, RF entries allocated from free list not sequentially, no data copy on retirement
alternatives_or_rejected: P6 scheme allocating data result registers and ROB entries as single wide entity with data and status field, with result physically copied from ROB data field into Retirement Register File (RRF) on retirement
rationale: Decoupling allows larger out-of-order window (126 uops in flight) and avoids copy overhead; NetBurst has much deeper buffering than P6 to allow looking at larger instruction window; separate allocation helps stall handling when RF unavailable
outcome: Can have 126 uops, 128 physical registers, 48 loads + 24 stores in flight simultaneously; retirement up to 3 uops per clock with proper exception handling and no move of data between structures

title: Rapid Execution Engine with double-clocked ALUs and multiple clock domains
where_in_paper: CLOCK RATES - different parts run at different frequencies and Execution Units
decision: Run highest frequency section (fast clock) at 2x main core clock equal to critical ALU-bypass loop for most integer programs; fast ALUs can schedule on each half of main clock (two operations per main clock), other parts run at half or quarter fast clock, bus logic at 100 MHz
alternatives_or_rejected: Single synchronous clock for entire chip at main frequency, which would make fast ALU loop timing limit entire chip frequency or require more stages everywhere
rationale: Staggered add and low-latency execution needed for integer performance; setting fast clock equal to ALU bypass loop speed and running rest of chip at half/quarter makes rest easier to design while still achieving high throughput; different frequency domains appropriate for performance needed
outcome: Two fast ALU dispatch ports (port 0 and port 1) dispatch up to two operations per main clock each, enabling higher execution throughput despite deeper pipeline

title: Large front-end BTB plus smaller Trace Cache BTB with advanced prediction
where_in_paper: Front End - ITLB and Front-End BTB, Trace Cache BTB
decision: Implement 4K-entry front-end BTB for Trace Cache misses plus 512-entry Trace Cache BTB for hits, both using highly advanced branch prediction algorithm that reduces misprediction rate by about 1/3 vs P6, with 16-entry return address stack and static backward-taken/forward-not-taken fallback
alternatives_or_rejected: Smaller BTB as in P6 or single predictor for both paths; paper notes front-end predictor must be large to capture most branch history for program, while Trace BTB can be smaller since it only predicts subset currently in Trace Cache
rationale: Accurate branch prediction critical because deeper 20-stage pipeline makes mispredict more expensive; front-end must steer fetch from L2 when Trace Cache misses, hardware prefetcher guided by BTB to keep decoder fed; return stack improves indirect return prediction for common call sites
outcome: Highly accurate speculation where predicted stream is usually accurate, enabling continuous high-bandwidth decoded uop stream and reduced front-end miss rate
